## Symptom

`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_atomic_completion_close.py::test_unrelated_remote_rejection_merges_and_rebuilds_private_candidate`
failed once in a full `make verify` run on macOS (Python 3.12.13, `PYTEST_WORKERS=4`, worker
`gw0`), and PASSES on its own (73 s, 1 passed) on the SAME tree immediately afterwards. So it
is order- or concurrency-sensitive, not a deterministic break.

## Evidence

```
tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_atomic_completion_close.py:41: in _run_git
    proc = subprocess.run(["git", *argv], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True)
E   subprocess.CalledProcessError: Command '['git', '-C', '<tmp>/test_unrelated_remote_rejectio0',
    'clone', '--quiet', '-b', 'tickets',
    '<tmp>/test_unrelated_remote_rejectio0/tickets-remote.git',
    '<tmp>/test_unrelated_remote_rejectio0/remote-writer']' returned non-zero exit status 128
```

The failing call is the test's own `_git(tmp_path, "clone", "--quiet", "-b", "tickets", …)` at
`test_atomic_completion_close.py:47`. `--quiet` means git's own diagnosis was DISCARDED, so the
128 has no cause attached — that is the first thing to fix, independently of the root cause.

## Why this needs a root cause, not a retry

`AGENTS.md`: a flaky test is a BUG to root-cause, never a retry. It is a regression oracle for
the atomic-completion close path; an intermittently red one erodes that. Exit 128 from
`clone -b <branch>` is most often "Remote branch tickets not found in upstream origin" — i.e. a
race in which the `tickets` branch is not yet present in the bare remote when the clone runs.
Under `-n 4 --dist worksteal` several lifecycle tests drive real git against per-test temp
remotes, so the hypothesis to test first is that the fixture creates the bare remote and pushes
`tickets` without a barrier the clone waits on. That is a hypothesis, NOT a finding: reproduce
it deterministically (`/rebar-debug`) before changing anything.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The `128` has a diagnosis: `_run_git` surfaces git's stderr on failure (drop `--quiet` on
      this call, or include `proc.stderr` in the raised message), so the next occurrence names
      its own cause instead of an exit code.
- [x] The failure is reproduced deterministically (a loop or a forced ordering under xdist) and
      the root cause is stated with a citation, before any fix.
- [x] The fixed test passes N consecutive full-suite runs at `PYTEST_WORKERS=4` with no
      recurrence; the fix addresses the CLASS (whatever ordering/barrier assumption is wrong),
      not this one test.

## Discovery

Seen while verifying story `friendless-alabaster-cub` (`4cfc-2de2-747d-4388`); that change
touches only `tests/unit/store/test_windows_exclusive_leg.py` and a `sweep (windows)` workflow
step and cannot reach this code path. Unrelated to it — filed so the flake is tracked rather
than re-run.
